key_insight: Large language models need explicit contextual belief management: they should update, retain, or ignore information depending on evidence, and vanilla prompting often fails at this.
engineering_relevance: For long-horizon AI systems, the results suggest that state management should be designed and trained explicitly, because reinforcement learning and representation steering can substantially improve reliability.
method: Introduced Contextual Belief Management (CBM) as a framework for belief update/retain/ignore decisions.
Built BeliefTrack, a closed-world benchmark with finite belief spaces and symbolic verifiers for exact turn-level scoring.
Compared vanilla LLMs, belief-tracking prompts, reinforcement learning with belief-state rewards, and representation-level steering.
evidence_signal: BeliefTrack evaluates turn-by-turn performance on two tasks—Rule Discovery and Circuit Diagnosis—and reports that RL with belief-state rewards reduces CBM failure rates by 70.9% on average.
watch_item: Because the benchmark is closed-world with symbolic verification, gains may not fully transfer to open-ended real-world settings where belief states are ambiguous and evidence is noisier.
paper_title: When Should Models Change Their Minds? Contextual Belief Management in Large Language Models
